Commentary.Commentary: Right then, when two juggernauts of the game collide, more often than not, we do get some exciting matches and series as well. That's exactly what has happened here and the series is nicely poised at 1-1 with one more game remaining. The caravan will now move from Darwin, where we have seen international cricket for the first time in 17 overs to Cairns for the final T20I. That game will be played on Saturday, 16 August and will begin at 9.15 am GMT. However, you can join us a lot sooner for the build-up. Till then, take care and goodbye!

Aiden Markram, the South African skipper, says that it was nice to take it to the third game and happy to get the win heading to Cairns. Lauds the knock of Dewald Brevis knock which right up there, says that he works hard and it was a freakish display of batting. Mentions that he is pleased with the knock as Brevis has played a lot of T20s and happy with his progress. Closes by sharing that Australia come hard with the bat, so they stuck to their strengths and bowled in the right areas.

Mitchell Marsh, the captain of Australia, has a bit of a chuckle when asked about Dewald Brevis and he says that he was saying to his teammates that Brevis mistimed a few sixes but he's a real up-and-coming talent, so kudos to him. Adds that chasing 219 was always going to be difficult and applauds South Africa for the way they played and is looking forward to the decider.

Dewald Brevis wins the PLAYER OF THE MATCH AWARD for his blistering knock. He says that he is grateful and happy that the team won. Shares that it’s great to be on the winning side. Says that the plan was to come back strong after the first game and everyone played their part well. Adds that Australia have a great squad and they hit the ball hard, so they had to be on their toes throughout the game.
The Presentation ceremony...

Earlier in the game, Mitchell Marsh won the toss and put South Africa into bat given the conditions seemed good for chasing with the dew coming into play as well. However, the Proteas got off to a bit of a flier in the Powerplay before losing their way for a bit. Ben Dwarshuis and Glenn Maxwell brought about a mini collapse before Dewald Brevis took center stage and played an unbelievable knock. It wasn't perfect as Brevis did get away with a few rash shots but more often than not, the ball-striking was sensational. Tristan Stubbs played a nifty hand too as Brevis finished with an unbeaten 125 off just 56 balls, helping his side pose a total well upwards of 200. As for Australia, Josh Hazlewood and Adam Zampa seemed a bit off color but Dwarshius kept up his form from the first game.

Tim David brought up a half-century in quick time but got out right after that as Kagiso Rabada got the all-important breakthrough for his side. Soon enough, it was a double whammy for the visitors as Glenn Maxwell fell in the very next over and the Aussies seemed down and out. There was a fightback from Alex Carey but that didn't last long and the Aussie tail couldn't wag as the Proteas kept on creating chances and made sure they held onto them as well. In the end, it was a comfortable victory, setting up the final game nicely.

218 is a daunting total on any surface and with a couple of early wickets, it becomes that more challenging for the chasing side even when there's plenty of dew. South Africa made sure they picked up those early wickets and it was their skipper, Aiden Markram, who got things rolling by dismissing Travis Head and then Kwena Maphaka got rid of Cameron Green to put the visitors on top. However, Tim David then came in and it seemed like he was going to hit every ball out of the park. He did get dropped again just like in the last game but couldn't punish the Proteas as much as last time.

South Africa have come roaring back in Darwin and have leveled up the T20I series at 1-1 with one more game remaining. It was a fine performance from the Proteas and they were just that bit better in all aspects of the game than Australia. Not only have South Africa broken the record-breaking run of 9 straight victories in T20Is for Australia but this is also Australia's second biggest loss in T20Is in Australia in terms of runs. Moreover, it is South Africa's biggest win in terms of runs over the Aussies.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! That has been nailed by Tim David! Banged in evern shorter now, over middle and leg, David gets on top of the bounce and massacres the pull shot down in front of deep backward square leg for another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Kwena Maphaka to Tim David, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Kwena Maphaka hurries the batter again but the line is wrong again. Short and around leg, David looks to flick but gets it off his gloves and the ball races away to the right of short fine leg for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Kwena Maphaka to Tim David, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Tim David is in next.

OUT! CAUGHT! Kwena Maphaka gets the last laugh in his battle with Cameron Green and Australia are 2 down inside 4 overs. Short of a length and at the body, skidding through. Green leans back to pull but hits it flat and hard, a bit uppish and to the right of mid-wicket. Nqabayomzi Peter takes a stellar diving catch, low down to his right and looks to celebrate wildly but the ball pops out of his hands. Thankfully for him, he had it in control for long enough and Green has to depart.
Commentary.Howout: c Nqabayomzi Peter b Kwena Maphaka
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Kwena Maphaka to Cameron Green, OUT! c Nqabayomzi Peter b Kwena Maphaka.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, did Nqabayomzi Peter hang on to the ball for long enough? Peter tried to throw it up in celebration but it spills out and the umpires have gone upstairs to have a look. The replays roll in and they do confirm that the ball was clearly caught and controlled. OUT comes up on the big screen.
FOUR! Bang! Back of a length and angled across off, Cameron Green stays back, clears the front leg and slam-dunks it right back over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Kwena Maphaka to Cameron Green, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! A skiddy short ball over leg stump, Green gets inside the line and manages to pull it fine of short fine leg for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Kwena Maphaka to Cameron Green, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! A false start from Kwena Maphaka. A lumbering run up from over the wicket and then comes that quick-arm action but this is angled well across the off stump for a wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Kwena Maphaka to Cameron Green, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length over middle, hit on the up and towards mid on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Lungi Ngidi to Cameron Green, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, that wasn't far away from the stumps! Ngidi keeps taking pace off and bowls it on a good length on off, angling it in. Cameron Green shimmies down the deck and looks to open up the off side but misses and the ball just goes over the stumps.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Lungi Ngidi to Cameron Green, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Another slower one, floated up fuller, Marsh is deceived by it and plays an uppish drive down to long on for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Lungi Ngidi to Mitchell Marsh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Takes pace off and angles it into the batter, Green looks to work it away but misses. The ball goes off the thigh pad and just into the leg side as the batters pick up an easy leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Lungi Ngidi to Cameron Green, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and outside off, Cameron Green rises up with the bounce and punches it down to cover-point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Lungi Ngidi to Cameron Green, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Length ball on the stumps, Marsh plants his front foot forward and hoicks it through wide mid on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Lungi Ngidi to Mitchell Marsh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Cameron Green walks in at number 3. Also, Lungi Ngidi replaces Kagiso Rabada in the attack.

OUT! CAUGHT! Excellent composure in the deep from Lhuan-dre Pretorius. Aiden Markram drops it a bit short and fires it in at the stumps. Travis Head rocks back again and pulls it in front of square but hits it flat. The ball seems to b sailing over but Pretorius tip-toes back, takes the catch and manages to slam the brakes just inside the ropes. Markram picks up a big early wicket for his side.
Commentary.Howout: c Lhuan-dre Pretorius b Aiden Markram
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Aiden Markram to Travis Head, OUT! c Lhuan-dre Pretorius b Aiden Markram.

Commentary.Commentary: Nagging length, attacking the off stump, Head rocks back to cut and gets it late towards short third.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Aiden Markram to Travis Head, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Very full again, drifted onto middle and leg, Marsh clears the front leg and drills it down to long off for another single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Aiden Markram to Mitchell Marsh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Around the wicket to the left-hander, bowled full and around off, driven away wide of long off for just one more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Aiden Markram to Travis Head, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Quicker and flatter, worked away off the back foot through mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Aiden Markram to Mitchell Marsh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Captain to captain and Mitchell Marsh deals the first blow. Fuller and angled into the pads, Marsh sits down and shovels the sweep with easy power over deep square leg for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Aiden Markram to Mitchell Marsh, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Aiden Markram to share the new ball with Kagiso Rabada.
Takes some pace off and bowls it back of a length outside off, Head stays leg side of the ball and reaches out to cut but is beaten. Australia are 7/0 after 1.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Kagiso Rabada to Travis Head, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nicely done in the end by Head. Good length on middle, just angling it away. Head watches it closer, lets the ball come on and opens the bat face to glide it wide of short third for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Kagiso Rabada to Travis Head, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Slower one, on a length and outside off, Head gets low and looks to hammer it through the off side but fails to connect.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Kagiso Rabada to Travis Head, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! A quick bumper over middle and leg, Travis Head looks to duck under it but has a late attempt at the ramp and misses. Wide called for height this time.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Kagiso Rabada to Travis Head, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! Banged in well short and well outside off, Travis Head leaves it alone and it is called a wide for being too far outside off. KG isn't thrilled with that call.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Kagiso Rabada to Travis Head, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! Pitched up outside off and angling it away, Head throws his hands at the ball but is comprehensively beaten.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Kagiso Rabada to Travis Head, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and in the channel around off, Travis Head hops back and punches it down towards cover-point but can't get it past the fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Kagiso Rabada to Travis Head, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Australia are underway right away! Hard length to begin with, at the pads, Mitchell Marsh fails to connect the pick-up shot and gets it off the legs towards fine leg for a leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Kagiso Rabada to Mitchell Marsh, Leg bye.
